subject: High LOD score with Permutation test

messages.author: 0656978e1d8a3229
messages.subject: High LOD score with Permutation test
parts:
Hello,

I am presently conducting QTL analysis in a tomato 8-way MAGIC population.

I have a quick question about setting the right threshold for QTL detection.

In fact the population is composed of 397 lines all of them genotyped for 1345 SNP that are discriminant among the 8 founder lines. 

A Bonferroni correction would give me a LOD score of 4.4. 

I used the scan1perm function to set an empirical threshold with 1000 permutation for different traits separately and I got a LOD score > 6 at 5% level most of the time. This threshold is a bit high from my perspective. So my question is, for traits where phenotypes is available for only a subset of the population, is the scan1perm the best option?

Thank you in advance.

I.Diouf

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl2-disc] High LOD score with Permutation test
parts:
Take a look at a histogram of the permutation results. If there's an odd 2nd mode in the right tail, then maybe there are some artifacts that are leading to high LOD threshold.

But generally, I would trust the permutation results more than I would analytical results with a Bonferroni correction. The permutation results are showing you what you get with data that you've ensured are completely random, with no QTL. And so if, with such data, you're getting LOD scores as high as 6 about 5% of the time, that seems pretty compelling to me.

How did you derive the Bonferonni-corrected LOD threshold of 4.4?

Me, I'd think that you'd be looking at LOD*2*ln(10) being chi-squared with 7 df at an individual point under the null hypothesis. So I'd look at

  qchisq(1 - 0.05/1345, 7) / 2 / log(10)

which gives about 7.0.

karl

Thank you Karl,

The histograms of the permutation didn’t look so strange so it seems to be right.

I calculated the Bonferroni LOD threshold like you did in the formula but I only used 2 df instead of 7 as I should.

I would probably continue the analysis with the permuted LOD as tha major known genes go above this threshold anyway.

Many thanks.

I.Diouf
